question: Which manner of death occurs without significant external force?
cited_learning_objective: List the 5 accepted possible manners of death in North Carolina.

options.rationale: Natural death occurs without significant external force.
Accident involves significant external force without intentional causation. It would apply to an unintentional traumatic death.
Homicide involves death caused through significant external force by another person. It would apply when another person's actions cause the death.
Suicide involves significant external force directed by the deceased. It would apply to an intentionally self-inflicted death.
Undetermined is used when the available investigation does not establish another manner. It would apply when the circumstances remain unresolved.

question: A wound has irregular margins, abraded edges, tissue bridges, and devitalized tissue. Which injury type best fits these findings?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the various types of force injuries/trauma (asphyxia; blunt trauma: contusion, abrasion, laceration, fractures and pressure/blast injury; sharp trauma; gunshot wounds).

options.rationale: An incised wound has clean margins and tissue cleaved into its depths. It would fit a sharp injury that is longer than it is deep.
A stab wound is a sharp-force injury that is deeper than it is long. It would fit penetration by a pointed object.
A blunt laceration results from crushing or tearing and characteristically has irregular, abraded margins with tissue bridges.
An abrasion is a superficial injury produced by tangential force. It would fit scraped skin that marks contact with a surface.
A contusion results from ruptured vessels with blood escaping into tissue. It would fit bruising without the described tissue separation.

question: Which wound feature most strongly supports a projectile exit site rather than an entrance site?
cited_learning_objective: Compare/contrast gunshot entrance and exit wounds.

options.rationale: A round or elliptical configuration commonly characterizes an entrance. It would support an entrance when accompanied by marginal abrasion.
Marginal abrasion is an entrance-wound feature. It would support the site where the projectile entered.
Stippling reflects powder reaching skin around an entrance. It would support a close or intermediate range entrance.
Wipe-off may occur at an entrance as material is deposited from the projectile. It would not support an exit site.
Exit wounds may be irregular or slit-like and characteristically lack marginal abrasion and wipe-off.

question: Which death is within the investigative and certification duties of a North Carolina medical examiner?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the duties of a NC medical examiner.

options.rationale: An expected medically attended natural death does not match the specified categories. Medical examiner jurisdiction would fit if the death were unattended or suspicious.
Medical examiners investigate and certify unattended apparently natural deaths as well as unnatural and suspicious deaths.
A routine monitored hospital death is medically attended and lacks the specified suspicious or traumatic circumstance. Jurisdiction would fit if the death became suspicious.
A scheduled witnessed hospice death is attended and expected. Medical examiner involvement would fit if an external force or suspicious circumstance emerged.
A documented expected disease death is not unattended, unnatural, or suspicious. It would fit medical examiner investigation if the circumstances were unexpected or unclear.

question: Two objects strike tissue at the same velocity, but one has substantially greater mass. Which consequence is expected from the stated energy relationship?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the various types of force injuries/trauma (asphyxia; blunt trauma: contusion, abrasion, laceration, fractures and pressure/blast injury; sharp trauma; gunshot wounds).

options.rationale: This is the correct physical consequence of increasing mass at unchanged velocity, but it does not itself describe the resulting injury effect.
Greater energy does not predict reduced deformation. Reduced deformation would be favored by less energy or wider force distribution.
Injury likelihood is related to the quantity of energy involved. It would remain unchanged only if the relevant energy were unchanged.
At the same velocity, greater mass produces greater kinetic energy, increasing the likelihood and potential degree of injury.
Greater mass at unchanged velocity increases rather than lowers kinetic energy. Lower transfer would fit an interaction with less involved energy.

question: The same impact force is redistributed over a wider area and a longer interval. Which outcome best follows?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the various types of force injuries/trauma (asphyxia; blunt trauma: contusion, abrasion, laceration, fractures and pressure/blast injury; sharp trauma; gunshot wounds).

options.rationale: Spreading impact over a wider area and longer period can avert or lessen injury by reducing force concentration.
Penetration is promoted when force is concentrated enough to overcome tissue resistance. It would fit a smaller area of force application.
Wider and longer force distribution lessens rather than accelerates tissue disruption. Disruption would increase with concentrated energy.
Focal deformation is caused by concentrated force. It would be favored by a narrow impact area.
Damage to deeper tissues becomes more likely after concentrated force overcomes resistance and penetrates. Wider distribution opposes that sequence.

question: A tissue sample is exposed to prolonged oxygen deprivation without direct mechanical impact. Which tissue is expected to be least resistant?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the various types of force injuries/trauma (asphyxia; blunt trauma: contusion, abrasion, laceration, fractures and pressure/blast injury; sharp trauma; gunshot wounds).

options.rationale: Muscle is among the tissues most resistant to ischemic or hypoxic injury. It would be more vulnerable only in a comparison involving still more resistant tissue.
Skin is among the tissues most resistant to oxygen deprivation. It would not be the first tissue expected to sustain irreversible hypoxic damage.
The brain is the least resistant listed tissue to ischemic or hypoxic injury because it is highly dependent on oxygen.
Heart has intermediate resistance to ischemic or hypoxic injury. It would be less resistant than bone, skin, or muscle but more resistant than brain.
Liver has intermediate resistance to oxygen deprivation. It would not be least resistant when cerebral tissue is included.

question: An injury reproduces the outline of the object that contacted the body. Which concept best describes this relationship?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the various types of force injuries/trauma (asphyxia; blunt trauma: contusion, abrasion, laceration, fractures and pressure/blast injury; sharp trauma; gunshot wounds).

options.rationale: A complex injury combines more than one injury mechanism, such as cutting and crushing. It would fit an ax or machete wound with sharp and blunt components.
An injury pattern is a predictable group of injuries produced by a trauma situation. It would fit the combined injuries expected in a fall or crash.
A tangential abrasion is a superficial scrape caused by force across the skin. It would fit road rash rather than an object's reproduced outline.
An internal contusion is blood extravasation within deeper tissue. It would fit ruptured vessels without requiring a recognizable object outline.
A patterned injury has an appearance that reflects the nature or shape of the causative object or force.

question: A superficial skin defect follows sliding contact across a rough surface. Which force direction and injury pairing is most appropriate?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the various types of force injuries/trauma (asphyxia; blunt trauma: contusion, abrasion, laceration, fractures and pressure/blast injury; sharp trauma; gunshot wounds).

options.rationale: Compression can disrupt bone and produce a fracture. It would fit bone injury rather than superficial scraped skin.
Abrasions are usually superficial skin injuries caused by tangential forces and indicate contact with a surface.
Crushing can tear tissue and produce a laceration with irregular margins and tissue bridges. It would fit a deeper split wound.
Sharp force produces cleanly cleaved margins without edge abrasion. It would fit a cut rather than a scrape.
Vascular rupture causes blood to escape into surrounding tissue and produces a contusion. It would fit discoloration without epidermal scraping.

question: A sharp-force wound measures farther across the skin than it extends into the tissue. Which classification is most appropriate?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the various types of force injuries/trauma (asphyxia; blunt trauma: contusion, abrasion, laceration, fractures and pressure/blast injury; sharp trauma; gunshot wounds).

options.rationale: A stab wound is deeper than it is long. It would fit penetration that extends farther into tissue than across skin.
A blunt laceration results from crushing or tearing and has irregular, abraded margins. It would not have the characteristic clean sharp-force margins.
An abrasion is a superficial scrape produced by tangential force. It would fit epidermal surface injury rather than clean tissue cleavage.
An incised wound is a sharp-force injury that is longer along the skin than it is deep.
A contusion is hemorrhage into tissue from ruptured vessels. It would fit bruising rather than an open sharp-force wound.

question: A bone breaks at a site weakened by pre-existing disease despite no traumatic event. Which fracture classification applies?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the various types of force injuries/trauma (asphyxia; blunt trauma: contusion, abrasion, laceration, fractures and pressure/blast injury; sharp trauma; gunshot wounds).

options.rationale: A pathologic fracture occurs at a site weakened by pre-existing pathology and may occur without trauma.
A compound fracture is associated with broken skin. It would fit an open fracture regardless of the bone's prior strength.
A comminuted fracture is splintered into multiple fragments. It would fit fragmentation rather than disease-related weakening.
A greenstick fracture is incomplete, with the bone cracked but not fully disrupted. It would fit incomplete traumatic failure.
A complete fracture fully disrupts the bone but does not identify pre-existing weakening. It would fit complete separation after force.

question: A firearm barrel has spiral grooves that rotate a single elongated projectile. Which performance effect follows from this design?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the various types of force injuries/trauma (asphyxia; blunt trauma: contusion, abrasion, laceration, fractures and pressure/blast injury; sharp trauma; gunshot wounds).

options.rationale: Pellet dispersal is associated with shotguns that usually fire multiple round projectiles. It would fit a smooth-bored weapon at increasing range.
The stated role of spiral grooves is rotational stability, not reduction of velocity. This would require a separate change affecting projectile speed.
Rifling imparts rotation that gives the projectile greater ballistic stability and therefore greater accuracy.
Multiple projectile release characterizes typical shotgun discharge. It would fit a smooth-bored firearm rather than a rifled weapon.
Rotational stability increases rather than reduces accuracy. Reduced accuracy would contradict the stated purpose of rifling.

question: Powder material is found within a projectile wound rather than on the surrounding skin. Which firing range is best supported?
cited_learning_objective: Compare/contrast gunshot entrance and exit wounds.

options.rationale: At distant range, powder residues fail to reach the body. It would fit an entrance without soot, stippling, or powder deposition.
At intermediate range, powder residues are visible on skin around the wound. It would fit external stippling rather than residue within the wound.
The described residue location provides usable range information. Indeterminate range would fit when the available wound findings do not establish a category.
With the gun against the body, discharge residue is deposited within the wound, supporting contact range.
At greater shotgun distance, pellet spread rather than residue within the wound is useful. Residue within the wound supports contact discharge.

question: A blast produces a shock wave, flying environmental fragments, and heat. Which description best integrates the resulting trauma?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the various types of force injuries/trauma (asphyxia; blunt trauma: contusion, abrasion, laceration, fractures and pressure/blast injury; sharp trauma; gunshot wounds).

options.rationale: Pressure effects represent only one component of the described event. This would fit a shock wave without penetrating debris or thermal exposure.
Penetrating fragments explain only one component. This would fit projectile injury without pressure or heat effects.
Thermal injury accounts only for heat or fire. This would fit a burn without shock-wave or fragment injury.
A simple blunt injury does not encompass the pressure, penetrating, and thermal components. It would fit a single non-sharp impact.
Blast events can combine pressure disruption, penetrating injury from fragments, and thermal injury from heat or fire.

question: A wound produced by a heavy edged tool shows both clean tissue division and crushed margins. Which interpretation best accounts for these findings?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the various types of force injuries/trauma (asphyxia; blunt trauma: contusion, abrasion, laceration, fractures and pressure/blast injury; sharp trauma; gunshot wounds).

options.rationale: An abrasion is a superficial injury from tangential force and does not explain clean division plus crushing. It would fit scraped skin.
An edged heavy object can both cut and crush, producing a complex injury with sharp and blunt components.
A contusion reflects blood escaping from ruptured vessels and does not explain divided tissue. It would fit bruising without an open wound.
A purely penetrating mechanism does not account for the combined cutting and crushing features. It would fit entry into tissue without the described mixed margins.
A simple blunt laceration explains crushed and torn margins but not clean tissue division. It would fit irregular margins with tissue bridges.

question: A 37-year-old man is found dead at home without medical attendance. No traumatic injury is visible, and the circumstances do not establish a disease process. Which action is most consistent with the responsible official's duties?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the duties of a NC medical examiner.

options.rationale: The death was unattended and its cause is not established, so immediate certification as expected natural death is unsupported. That action would fit a documented, attended disease death.
Unattended apparently natural deaths fall within medical examiner investigation. Deferral would fit a medically attended expected death without suspicious circumstances.
Accident requires an unintentional death involving significant external force, which has not been established. It would fit a documented unintentional traumatic event.
Medical examiners investigate and certify unattended apparently natural deaths, including cases requiring clarification of cause and manner.
Undetermined is a manner, not a cause, and investigation should precede its use. It would apply as the manner if the completed investigation could not establish another category.

question: A 25-year-old unrestrained driver strikes a rigid barrier. A sharply outlined mark matching the steering apparatus is present on the abdomen. Which interpretation is most appropriate?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the various types of force injuries/trauma (asphyxia; blunt trauma: contusion, abrasion, laceration, fractures and pressure/blast injury; sharp trauma; gunshot wounds).

options.text: The mark identifies a patterned injury
options.rationale: The individual mark reflects the nature and shape of the object that caused it, meeting the definition of a patterned injury.

options.text: The mark establishes an injury pattern
options.rationale: An injury pattern is a predictable collection of injuries produced by a trauma situation. It would apply to the combined injuries expected in an unrestrained collision.

options.text: The mark confirms a sharp injury
options.rationale: Sharp injury requires clean margins and tissue cleavage. It would fit contact with an edged or pointed object rather than a steering apparatus.

options.text: The mark proves an accidental manner
options.rationale: The mark identifies an object-force relationship but does not alone establish the circumstances required for manner classification. Accident would require evidence that the event was unintentional.

options.text: The mark demonstrates an incised wound
options.rationale: An incised wound is longer than it is deep and has sharp, clean margins. It would fit a cutting instrument rather than blunt imprinting.

question: A 42-year-old person is reported to have fallen down several steps. Examination shows numerous similarly shaped injuries matching repeated blows rather than scattered scrapes and bruises. Which conclusion is best supported?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the various types of force injuries/trauma (asphyxia; blunt trauma: contusion, abrasion, laceration, fractures and pressure/blast injury; sharp trauma; gunshot wounds).

options.text: The findings support an ordinary fall
options.rationale: Falls down stairs typically produce scrapes, bruises, occasional lacerations, and sometimes fractures. Repeated recognizable shapes do not fit that nonspecific pattern.
Sharp-force trauma produces cleanly cleaved margins without edge abrasion. It would fit cuts or stabs rather than repeated blunt imprints.
Recognizable patterned injuries are suspicious for inflicted trauma, whereas unintentional injuries tend to produce nonspecific patterns.

Natural death occurs without significant external force, but the injuries indicate repeated external force. Natural manner would require death from disease without a significant traumatic contribution.
Distant gunfire is assessed by absent powder residue and projectile-wound characteristics. It would require gunshot defects rather than repeated blunt shapes.

question: A 19-year-old motorcyclist slides across pavement. Examination shows broad superficial skin loss over the lateral arm without deep tissue separation. Which finding would most directly identify the contact site?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the various types of force injuries/trauma (asphyxia; blunt trauma: contusion, abrasion, laceration, fractures and pressure/blast injury; sharp trauma; gunshot wounds).

options.rationale: An internal contusion reflects vessel rupture within deeper tissue and does not directly mark surface contact. It would fit internal blunt impact.
A complete fracture indicates full bone disruption but does not directly localize sliding contact. It would fit sufficient compression, bending, or twisting.
An incised defect results from sharp cutting and has clean margins. It would identify contact with a sharp edge rather than pavement sliding.
Abrasions result from tangential surface contact and forensically indicate where the body contacted the surface.
A stab wound is deeper than it is long and results from a pointed object. It would identify penetrating sharp-force contact.

question: A 6-year-old child has a swollen purple skin lesion after blunt impact. Yellow discoloration is confined to the periphery. Which interpretation is most appropriate?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the various types of force injuries/trauma (asphyxia; blunt trauma: contusion, abrasion, laceration, fractures and pressure/blast injury; sharp trauma; gunshot wounds).

options.text: The lesion is a fresh abrasion
options.rationale: An abrasion is superficial scraped skin rather than blood within tissue. It would fit tangential contact with surface disruption.

options.text: The lesion is an old laceration
options.rationale: A laceration is torn or crushed tissue with irregular margins and tissue bridges. It would fit an open wound rather than discoloration.

options.text: The lesion is a sharp incision
options.rationale: An incision has clean margins and tissue cleaved into depth. It would fit a cutting instrument rather than blunt discoloration.

options.text: The lesion precisely dates the impact
options.rationale: Bruise color provides only a rough age estimate because size, vascularity, and pigmentation affect appearance. Precise dating is not supported.

options.text: The lesion is an evolving contusion
options.rationale: A swollen red-blue to purple lesion with peripheral yellowing fits a contusion undergoing early color evolution.

question: A 30-year-old man has a scalp wound after being struck with a blunt object. The margins appear irregular and abraded. Which additional finding would best confirm the same injury mechanism?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the various types of force injuries/trauma (asphyxia; blunt trauma: contusion, abrasion, laceration, fractures and pressure/blast injury; sharp trauma; gunshot wounds).

options.rationale: Tissue bridges are characteristic of a laceration produced by crushing or tearing from blunt force.
Clean tissue cleavage supports sharp trauma. It would fit an incised or stab wound without tissue bridges.
Powder particles around a wound support a close or intermediate gunshot entrance. They would require firearm discharge near the body.
Wipe-off may occur at a projectile entrance. It would fit transfer from a bullet entering tissue rather than blunt tearing.
Clean edges without abrasion characterize sharp trauma. They would fit cutting by a sharp instrument.

question: A 28-year-old man is found with a narrow wound made by a pointed screwdriver. The defect extends farther into the body than across the skin. Which classification best fits?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the various types of force injuries/trauma (asphyxia; blunt trauma: contusion, abrasion, laceration, fractures and pressure/blast injury; sharp trauma; gunshot wounds).

options.rationale: An incised wound is longer than it is deep. It would fit a cutting motion across the skin.
A stab wound is deeper than it is long and may be produced by a pointed object even when the point is not sharply edged.
A blunt laceration results from crushing or tearing and has irregular abraded margins with tissue bridges. It would fit blunt impact over firm tissue.
An abrasion is superficial and results from tangential force. It would fit scraping rather than deep penetration.
A contusion is blood extravasation into tissue after vessel rupture. It would fit bruising rather than a penetrating defect.

question: A 54-year-old worker is injured in an explosion. He has disrupted internal organs, embedded environmental fragments, and burns. Which mechanism accounts for the full injury combination?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the various types of force injuries/trauma (asphyxia; blunt trauma: contusion, abrasion, laceration, fractures and pressure/blast injury; sharp trauma; gunshot wounds).

options.rationale: Tangential force produces abrasions or tearing but does not explain pressure disruption and thermal injury. It would fit sliding surface contact.
Sharp force may explain tissue cutting but not shock-wave disruption and burns. It would fit wounds from knives, glass, or similar edges.
Thermal exposure explains burns but not embedded fragments or pressure effects. It would fit heat or fire without blast components.
Explosion injuries can combine shock-wave pressure effects, penetrating environmental fragments, and thermal injury.
Direct compression may disrupt tissue or bone but does not account for penetrating fragments and burns. It would fit a crushing event.

question: A 46-year-old woman sustains complete interruption of cerebral blood supply. She rapidly loses awareness, but circulation is restored before several minutes pass. Which time-dependent event occurred first?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the various types of force injuries/trauma (asphyxia; blunt trauma: contusion, abrasion, laceration, fractures and pressure/blast injury; sharp trauma; gunshot wounds).

options.rationale: Irreversible brain injury occurs after approximately 3-4 minutes of acute cerebral blood-flow interruption. It would fit a longer interruption.
The liver is more resistant to hypoxic injury than the brain, and this is not the earliest described event. It would require a longer period of oxygen deprivation.
Acute interruption of cerebral blood supply causes unconsciousness after approximately 6-10 seconds, before irreversible brain injury develops.
Muscle is relatively resistant to ischemic or hypoxic injury. Irreversible muscular injury would require more prolonged deprivation than rapid loss of awareness.
Skin is relatively resistant to ischemic or hypoxic injury. Permanent skin injury would not precede the brain's rapid functional failure.

question: A 40-year-old man is struck in the head during a fight, remains conscious, drives away, and is later found dead. Examination shows a depressed skull defect with bleeding beneath it. Which principle best explains the delayed fatal outcome despite limited external injury?
cited_learning_objective: Verbally describe and visually identify the various types of force injuries/trauma (asphyxia; blunt trauma: contusion, abrasion, laceration, fractures and pressure/blast injury; sharp trauma; gunshot wounds).

options.rationale: Limited external injury does not exclude serious internal damage. This principle would apply only if surface findings reliably reflected deeper injury, which they do not here.
Tangential force explains abrasions but not the depressed fracture and internal bleeding. It would fit road rash or a surface scrape.
Sharp force produces clean margins without abrasion. It would fit a cut or stab rather than blunt cranial impact.
Bone is relatively resistant compared with other tissues, but sufficient force can fracture it. Absolute resistance would contradict the observed depressed defect.

options.text: Internal disruption may impair vital function
options.rationale: Mechanical trauma can cause fracture, vascular injury, and internal organ damage whose functional consequences are severe despite minimal external findings.

question: A 33-year-old person has two projectile defects. One is round with a narrow abraded rim and wipe-off; the other is irregular without an abraded rim. Which designation is most appropriate for the first defect?
cited_learning_objective: Compare/contrast gunshot entrance and exit wounds.

options.rationale: A round or elliptical defect with marginal abrasion and possible wipe-off characterizes a gunshot entrance.
Exit wounds are often irregular or slit-like and lack marginal abrasion and wipe-off. That classification fits the second defect.
A graze differs from the described penetrating defect with a circumferential abraded margin. It would fit a projectile passing tangentially across the surface.
A blunt laceration has irregular abraded edges, tissue bridges, and devitalized tissue. It would arise from crushing or tearing rather than projectile entry.
An incised wound has sharp clean margins and is longer than it is deep. It would fit a cutting edge rather than a projectile.

question: A 29-year-old man has a firearm wound with soot and punctate powder marks on the skin surrounding the defect. Which range classification is best supported?
cited_learning_objective: Compare/contrast gunshot entrance and exit wounds.

options.rationale: Contact discharge places residue within the wound because the gun is against the body. It would fit internal residue rather than surrounding stippling.
At distant range, residues fail to reach the body. It would fit absence of soot, stippling, and powder particles.
Soot, stippling, tattooing, or powder particles on skin around the wound support close or intermediate firing range.
The surrounding powder effects provide affirmative range evidence. Indeterminate classification would fit when such distinguishing findings are unavailable.
A remote shotgun wound is assessed through pellet spread and would not retain prominent surrounding powder effects. It would fit widely dispersed pellets.

question: A 41-year-old hunter has a shotgun wound with a central defect and several separate surrounding pellet defects. Which factor is most useful for estimating firing distance?
cited_learning_objective: Compare/contrast gunshot entrance and exit wounds.

options.rationale: Bruise color can only roughly estimate contusion age and does not determine shotgun range. It would be relevant to aging a separate blunt injury.
Tissue bridges characterize blunt lacerations rather than shotgun range. They would support crushing or tearing.
Incised margins identify sharp-force cutting and do not estimate firearm distance. They would fit a blade injury.
In shotgun wounds, increasing pellet spread and the appearance of satellite wounds provide useful information about firing distance.
Devitalized tissue is a feature of laceration and does not specifically estimate shotgun range. It would support blunt tearing.

question: A 35-year-old man has one projectile defect that is smaller and round and another that is larger and irregular. Which finding is required before confidently identifying the smaller defect as the entrance?
cited_learning_objective: Compare/contrast gunshot entrance and exit wounds.

options.rationale: Size alone is unreliable because an entrance may be smaller than an exit. Marginal abrasion specifically supports an entrance site.
An irregular or slit-like outline favors an exit rather than an entrance. It would support the larger defect if marginal abrasion were absent.
Absence of marginal abrasion supports an exit. It would make the smaller defect less characteristic of an entrance.
Exit-wound edges may approximate without tissue loss. This finding would support an exit rather than establish entrance.
Wipe-off may be present at an entrance, whereas its absence is characteristic of an exit. Absence would not confirm the smaller defect as entrance.

question: A 62-year-old woman dies after a fracture occurs through bone weakened by cancer without a traumatic event. Which manner is best supported if the disease process alone produced death?
cited_learning_objective: List the 5 accepted possible manners of death in North Carolina.

options.rationale: Accident involves significant external force producing an unintentional death. It would apply if an unintended traumatic event caused the fatal fracture.
The fracture arose from pre-existing disease without significant external force, so a disease-driven natural manner is supported.
Homicide requires fatal external force caused by another person. It would fit an inflicted traumatic fracture.
Suicide requires intentional self-inflicted external force. It would fit a fatal injury deliberately caused by the deceased.
Undetermined is used when investigation cannot establish another manner. It would fit unresolved circumstances rather than a death explained by disease alone.

question: A 24-year-old man dies after intentionally producing a fatal external-force injury to himself. Which manner of death is most appropriate?
cited_learning_objective: List the 5 accepted possible manners of death in North Carolina.

options.rationale: Natural death occurs without significant external force. It would fit death caused solely by disease.
Accident involves an unintentional externally caused death. It would fit a traumatic event without intent to cause the fatal injury.
Homicide applies when another person causes death through external force. It would fit an inflicted fatal injury by someone else.
Intentional self-infliction of the fatal external force supports classification as suicide.
Undetermined applies when the investigation cannot resolve the manner. It would fit unclear evidence regarding intent or causation.

question: A 48-year-old person dies from a traumatic injury, but the completed investigation cannot determine whether the force was accidental, self-inflicted, or inflicted by another. Which manner is most appropriate?
cited_learning_objective: List the 5 accepted possible manners of death in North Carolina.

options.rationale: Natural death occurs without significant external force, whereas this death is traumatic. It would fit a disease process without a significant external contribution.
Accident requires support that the fatal external force was unintentional. It would fit established unintentional trauma.
Homicide requires support that another person caused the fatal injury. It would fit an established inflicted death.
Suicide requires support for intentional self-infliction. It would fit a fatal injury deliberately caused by the deceased.
Undetermined is appropriate when the investigation cannot resolve the death among the other recognized manners.
